newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds leads banks higher, Capel positive.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds leads banks higher, Capel positive.

text.p: Shares in Lloyds TSB Plc led UK banks higher on Tuesday as analysts at HSBC James Capel repeated an "overweight" stance on the sector and said recent falls were overdone.

In a 44-page review of recent results in the bank sector, Capel analyst Michael Lever said the dramatic falls of the past week on interest rate fears were overdone and that prospective rate increases should do little damage to bank profits.
Lever's favourite stocks in the sector are Lloyds TSB and HSBC Holdings Plc.
Lloyds shares were up 22-1/2p or five percent at 476-1/2 -- the biggest gain in the FTSE 100 index -- and HSBC was up 25p at 15.01 stg.

Elsewhere in the sector Barclays Plc was up 22-1/2p at 10.13 stg, National Westminster Bank Plc was up 16-1/2p at 693, Bank of Scotland Plc was up 7-1/2p at 321 and Royal Bank of Scotland Plc up 5p at 520-1/2.
Dealers said the sector was due a rally after recent falls and pointed out that Lloyds had suffered one of the biggest declines.

"Lloyds came off more than most of the other banks. There was a split order around this morning and it didn't take much to move them back," said one senior sales trader. "They had seen a significant downward move since last Wednesday."
